decisions.where: The opening line under the title: `invoicer` gives the `accountant` a command that prints a client's invoice from the invoice lines that the `accountant` keeps in a spreadsheet, at that client's tax rate.
Roles, the `installer` line: a developer who sets up `invoicer`'s command on each `accountant`'s machine, installing Python and `invoicer` in place of the `accountant`.
Roles: the first line, `invoicer` serves two roles, and the `accountant` and `installer` items.

The whole vision: `invoicer` for the product, `invoicer`'s command for what is run, `accountant` for one who prints, and the `accountant`'s machine for where it runs, each written the same way throughout.
Objectives and key results, the `O1` item.
Objectives and key results, the `O2` item.
Objectives and key results: the tasks the key results measure, from opening the spreadsheet to the printed invoice (`KR1.2`) and from starting a setup to `invoicer`'s command running (`KR2.2`).

Objectives and key results: `KR1.1`, `KR1.2`, `KR2.1`, `KR2.2` with Lower is better; the ranking line, `KR1.1` before `KR1.2` and `KR2.1` before `KR2.2`; and the no-targets line with its plain reason.

Objectives and key results: O1 is the `accountant`'s and O2 the `installer`'s, so the command and the README's part for the `accountant` serve O1 and the README's setup section serves O2; the vision lists no README pieces, which the README's own points settle.

Concept, its first line: the `accountant` gives `invoicer`'s command the invoice lines as the `accountant`'s spreadsheet already holds them, plus the client's tax rate, and `invoicer` prints the finished invoice.
Concept, the three ideas: The spreadsheet as it is, Nothing wrong prints, and The rate given each time.

Concept, the lines under each idea: the `installer` sets up no format and no rates; each time the `accountant` prints an invoice, they give the client's tax rate; `invoicer` prints nothing where it can't read a line or the rate, its message says what to fix, and the `accountant` fixes it and runs the command again.

more.where: The opening line under the title says that `invoicer` gives the `accountant` a command, before Roles, so `KR2.1` speaks of a command the reader already knows.
Objectives and key results, the ranking line: `KR1.1` ranks before `KR1.2`, and `KR2.1` ranks before `KR2.2`, followed by the keep rule.

Objectives and key results: the ranking and the keep rule, and the no-targets rule and its reason, each in sentences of their own, with no plural subject and comes; Concept: each idea's lines, one point to a sentence, one for the `accountant` and one for the `installer`, and the unreadable-line idea in three sentences.

Concept: invoicer prints the finished invoice and prints nothing, in place of returns and the print; Objectives and key results, its first two lines: O and KR written out as objective and key result; the no-targets line: the plain reason, with the name Goodhart's law dropped.

The whole vision: `invoicer` in code format each time, `invoicer`'s command in place of the command, each `accountant`'s machine in place of the accounting team's machines, and `accountant` and `installer` in code format each time.

settled.decided: As one line under the title, before Roles.
settled.ground: The template has no place for the job, and refactor-doc N3 asks that a reader know invoicer is a command before KR2.1, so it comes first.
